answer: Each round the ledger hands every account a private salt and later quizzes it on three past salts. An honest agent keeps one small journal; a farm of 1,000 fakes must store and route 1,000 separate histories without letting answers wander between accounts. One crossed reply in any gale of random audits slashes that account's stake, and since salts are never shared, colluding operators cannot pool memory. The cost rises with every account, like a tide that never ebbs.
